note: The prose of the three race-engineering prompts. DATA, NOT CODE: edit the wording here without touching pitcrew/prompts/build.py, and bump `version` when you do. The version travels in every generated footer and is stored with every issued prompt, so a returned setup sheet is traceable to the template that asked for it. Prompts A and B are ports of buildBrief() and buildLog() in reference/gt7-race-engineering.html and their wording is tuned for the knowledge base that reads them — it is not to be 'improved'. Only where the values come from changed. {braces} are filled by the builder.

shared.rangesRuleBrief: **Every recommended value must fall inside these ranges.** Give each suspension value as absolute number + clicks from minimum + % of range, so it survives if the real range differs. Do not recommend a value at a hard limit unless you say why the limit is the right answer.

shared.returnHeading: ## How to send the sheets back
shared.returnLead: Give me the readable sheets above **and** one fenced `json` block at the very end, in exactly the shape below. I read the prose and argue with it; Pit Crew reads the JSON and enters the values. Without it I retype every number by hand, which is where transcription errors come from - so this is in addition to the readable sheets, never instead of them.
returnShape: "sheetName": "<short name I can pick out of a list>",
"testFirst": ["<first thing to try if the car is still not right>"]
shared.returnVocabHeading: **`values` keys — this list and no other:**
shared.returnQualiRule: Two sheets, both in `sheets`, tagged `race` and `qualifying`. They are separate objects in Pit Crew and are practised separately, so send the qualifying one even when it is the race sheet with three values moved - and if the diagnosis does not move it at all, send it unchanged and say so rather than leaving it out. A missing sheet reads as "no answer", not as "no change".
returnRulesBrief: - One block, last thing in the reply, fenced as ```json.

- **Every setting on the sheet, every time.** This is the first sheet for this combination, so there is no previous one to fall back on and a key you leave out is a value Pit Crew has nothing to enter. Send `null` for a setting the car does not have; send the number for everything it does, including the ones you are leaving at the baseline.
- `values` keys are the vocabulary below and nothing else.
- Numbers as numbers. No units, no `+`, no quotes: `-2.4`, not `"-2.4 deg"`.

- **Camber is a positive magnitude in GT7**, unlike every other sim: the in-game slider runs from 0.0 upward and the app refuses a negative one, because it is a slider position I cannot enter. Only toe and brake balance take a sign.
- `null` for a setting this car does not have. Never `0` - zero is a real value on camber, toe and ballast, and a null read as zero is a setup change nobody asked for.
- `gears` is 1st..nth in order. The final drive is `fg` in `values` like any other setting, not a field of its own - one place per number, or a reply can say two different things at once.
- `why` is keyed the same as `values`, one short line each. It is what makes the change auditable a month later; a sheet with no reasons is a sheet nobody can argue with.
- If a value had to be clamped to a slider limit, list it in `clamped` and say so in the prose too.

brief.title: # GT7 SETUP BRIEF
brief.standing: Generate a **race setup sheet** and a **qualifying setup sheet** in GT7 in-game layout for the following. Use the driver profile and playbook in the project. Express per-car suspension values as **percent of slider range plus clicks from minimum**, since GT7 ranges are car-specific. Send the sheets both ways: readable for me, and as the JSON block described at the end so Pit Crew can enter them.
brief.circuitUnknown: - **{circuit}** — not in the circuit reference. I have no length, corner count, downforce requirement, wear severity or pit-loss figure for it; work from the layout you know and say what you assumed.
brief.contextFirstRun: - First run of this combination — no previous sheet, session or lap on file.
required: 1. **Race sheet** and **Qualifying sheet**, side by side, GT7 in-game order and naming.
2. A short **why** for every value that deviates from the baseline sheet.
3. **Gearing** built from the actual longest straight and slowest corner at this circuit, not a target top speed.
4. **Strategy note**: expected stint length, stop window, fuel map, and the in-race brake-balance / TCS migration plan.
5. **Three things to test first** if the car is not right, in priority order.
brief.requiredRangeCheck: 6. A **range check** — confirm every value on both sheets sits inside the slider ranges above, and list anything you had to clamp.

refinement.title: # GT7 DRIVER FEEDBACK — SETUP REFINEMENT REQUEST
refinement.standing: I have run the setup you issued for this combination. Diagnose what the car did and reissue the sheet for the race. Work from the driver profile, playbook and change hierarchy in the project. The driver report below is primary evidence - read it literally rather than smoothing it into generic symptoms. Where it and the telemetry disagree, that disagreement is the finding: say which you are trusting and why, and do not average them.
refinement.setupNotRecorded: - No sheet was recorded against this session — use the sheet you issued for this combination and say which version you are working from.
refinement.symptomsNone: - Nothing flagged from the symptom list
refinement.dataDisagreement: Where the Pit Crew data and my report disagree, say so explicitly, say which you are trusting, and why. Do not quietly average them.
refinement.dataAbsent: **Not used this session.** Diagnose from the driver report alone. Where a call genuinely needs data I have not given you, say what to measure next time rather than guessing — and flag how confident you are in each change.
required: 1. **Diagnosis** — map each symptom to a cause, ranked by how much it is costing, and name the corner phase each belongs to. Say which symptoms are one problem wearing two faces.
2. **Revised race sheet** in full GT7 in-game layout, ready to enter by hand.
3. **Qualifying sheet** — reissue it only if the diagnosis moves it, and say so either way.
4. **Delta table**: parameter · as run · revised · why. Nothing changes without a reason.
5. **What each change should feel like**, so one run tells me whether it worked.
6. **What you deliberately left alone**, and why — the things that were working.
7. **Three things to try next**, in order, if the first revision is still not right.
refinement.hierarchy: Respect the change hierarchy — change the fewest things that will fix it, and where two changes are coupled, say so rather than shipping both silently.
refinement.returnQualiRule: Two sheets, both in `sheets`, tagged `race` and `qualifying`. They are separate objects in Pit Crew and are practised separately, so send the qualifying one even when it is the race sheet with three values moved - and if the diagnosis does not move it at all, send it unchanged and say so rather than leaving it out. A missing sheet reads as "no answer", not as "no change".

outcome.title: # GT7 EVENT OUTCOME — POST-MORTEM AND KNOWLEDGE-BASE UPDATE
outcome.standing: The event is complete. Diagnose the setup against what the car actually did, reissue the sheets for the next running of this combination, and update the knowledge base. The driver report below is primary evidence — read it literally rather than smoothing it into generic symptoms.
outcome.gearboxMismatch: **The gearbox in the car was not the gearbox on the sheet.** Telemetry read the fitted ratios and they do not match the sheet below. Treat every gearing-dependent finding here as suspect until that is resolved.
outcome.strategyAbsent: No strategy was approved for this event, so there is no plan to compare against. The stint and fuel figures below are what the race did, not what it was planned to do.
outcome.multiplierAssumed: - **`wearMeasuredAtRaceMultiplier: false`** — the wear rate behind this plan was not measured at the multiplier that was raced. Multiplier linearity is assumed and has never been demonstrated, so treat any converted stint length as unproven rather than measured.
outcome.callsAbsent: The engineer made no calls during this race.
outcome.callsLead: Every call the engineer made, including the ones I declined. A plan offered and refused is evidence about the model.
outcome.wearLead: **GT7 exposes no tyre wear channel in any packet format.** Everything below is modelled or read off the in-game gauge by hand, and carries its source. None of it is measured.
outcome.gearingLead: Read off the stream, not off the sheet. There is no tow figure and there never will be — GT7's feed carries no proximity or closing speed, so whether a top speed was set in a tow is in my notes or nowhere.
required: 1. **Post-mortem** — what the setup cost me over the event, ranked, mapped to corner phase.
2. **Revised race and qualifying sheets**, full GT7 in-game layout, both carried in the single JSON block described at the end.
3. **Delta table** — parameter · as run · revised · why.
4. **Strategy review** — was the binding constraint correctly identified, was the stint model right, which calls were right and which were wrong, and what changes in the model as a result.
5. **Knowledge-base updates, stated explicitly and separately**, so they can be filed:
- what to record about **this car**, including any newly measured slider ranges
- what to record about **this circuit** — pit loss, wear axle and severity, gearing constraints, the top three levers
- what to record about **this combination** specifically
- any **claim in the knowledge base this event contradicts** — the most valuable output of all, and the one that never appears unless it is asked for
- anything that should be **measured next session** to close an open question
6. **Confidence flags** on every item in 5 — measured, or inferred and needing a second event to confirm.
outcome.requiredEmphasis: Item 5 is why this prompt exists. Do not fold it into the post-mortem — state it separately, so it can be filed.
outcome.hierarchy: Respect the change hierarchy — change the fewest things that will fix it, and where two changes are coupled, say so rather than shipping both silently.
outcome.returnLeadExtra: This is a post-mortem, so the sheets are for the *next* running of this combination. Tag them the same way.
outcome.noRace: **No race was recorded for this event.** There are no laps, no stops and no calls to review, so there is nothing here to diagnose against. Do not reconstruct what probably happened - say what you would need recorded to answer this properly, and stop there.
